descriptionChirho: A person of Roman citizenship or identity, used as both a substantivized adjective ('a Roman') and a collective ethnic/political designation ('the Romans'). This single sense covers individual Roman citizenship claims (Paul asserting 'I am a Roman,' Acts 22:25-29, 23:27), collective references to Romans as a political group (John 11:48, 'the Romans will come'; Acts 16:21, 37-38, customs 'not lawful for Romans'; Acts 2:10, 'visitors from Rome'), and the Roman legal system (Acts 25:16, 'the custom of the Romans'; Acts 28:17, 'delivered into the hands of the Romans'). All multilingual glosses consistently translate with the same term for 'Roman' across all clusters, confirming there is no semantic distinction among these auto-generated splits.
